newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks close down on Dow, long bond rates.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks close down on Dow, long bond rates.

text.p: Mexican stocks gave up early gains to close lower Thursday on the back of a bearish Dow Jones and upside pressure on U.S. long bond rates, traders said.
"Pressure on the long bond increased after mid-session, pushed the Dow further down and affected the local market," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC index closed 23.27 points off, or 0.70 percent, to 3,306.72 points, close to psychological support at 3,300 points.
Volume was moderate at 92.4 million shares. Of 99 stocks traded, losers outnumbered winners, 48 to 31.

"June Industrial production figures in line with expectations and technical considerations shored up buying in early trade but jitters over long bond rates never quite went away," said a trader from the Obsa brokerage.

The Mexican Finance Ministry reported on Thursday that industrial output in June gained 12 percent compared to the year-ago figure. A trader from the Bancomer brokerage also said this was in line with market expectations.
Mexican stocks were under pressure, however, from U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rates that climbed to 7.15 percent when the bolsa closed, compared with 7.10 percent at Wednesday's close.
Higher long bond rates, lower bond prices, forced the Dow Jones down almost 50 points, or 0.88 percent, to 5,606.96.
"The bolsa was closely linked to U.S. developments, but I think it respected its support levels very well, where you could tell buyers entered the market," the Obsa trader added.
Traders estimated that the bolsa may fall again on Friday in reaction to U.S. payroll figures and long bond rates.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares suffered profit-taking, falling 26 centavos (3 cents) to 12.48 pesos ($1.64).
